network.tdh.spec.metadataDescription: The exact rule behind TDH: every input, formula and rounding step, in readable form.
network.tdh.spec.title: The TDH-v1 specification
network.tdh.spec.lede: TDH-v1 is the exact rule behind TDH, written so that independent programs produce identical results, to the last unit. It restates the formula 6529.io’s backend uses today; earlier boost schedules, listed under Historic boosts, differed. Where it departs from the backend, it removes a dependence on timing, database order, editable data or floating-point evaluation, and section 11 lists each departure with its measured effect.
network.tdh.spec.version: Rule version tdh-v1.0. This page follows specification P26 at commit f840096, its latest change (October 16, 2026). P26 is a proposal, not yet adopted as a consensus rule; by the owner’s decisions, 6529.io computes it from the cutover, about October 23, 2026, and every validator computes it once validators run.
network.tdh.spec.mapDesc: Inputs (section 2) feed canonical events (3), which set the snapshot (4). Eligibility and rates (5) and identities (6) both feed holdings (7), which feed scores (8) and the day’s output (9). The parameters (10) feed sections 5 to 8.
network.tdh.spec.s1.title: 1. Scope and conventions
network.tdh.spec.s1.body: TDH-v1 defines, for one day, each wallet’s and each identity’s balance, whole days, base, boost and final TDH for every eligible token, and the network totals. Ranks, xTDH, REP and upload files are out of scope. All arithmetic is on integers or exact fractions. Where the old backend’s floating-point rounding matters, the rule names it exactly: B64 is the nearest binary64 number, and it only decides ties. Every number and address the rule uses comes from the registry of the rule version (section 10): its contracts, the sinks, the length of a holding day, the season starts and the bonuses.
network.tdh.spec.s2.title: 2. Inputs
network.tdh.spec.s2.body: One day’s inputs are Ethereum’s canonical chain up to the snapshot block, every event of four contracts up to that block, the edition-floor state of a fifth contract read at that block, and the rule version’s parameter list. Prices, Meme Lab, received xTDH, REP and $6529 balances are not inputs.
network.tdh.spec.s2.tableCaption: Four event sources and one state read
network.tdh.spec.s2.delegationEvents: Register and revoke, direct and through a sub-delegate
network.tdh.spec.s2.manifoldEvents: getClaimForToken, read at the snapshot block
network.tdh.spec.s2.topicsCaption: Topic hashes, keccak-256 of each signature
network.tdh.spec.s3.title: 3. Canonical events
network.tdh.spec.s3.body: Every event is read exactly once, decoded strictly, and put in one order that everyone can reproduce: block, then transaction, then log, then position in a batch. A node that cannot show it has every event must not publish, and a malformed event invalidates the day’s input rather than being skipped.
network.tdh.spec.s3.sinks: A mint comes from the zero address to any other address and debits nobody; a transfer from the zero address to itself moves nothing and is not a mint. A transfer to a sink, the zero address or 0x…dead in tdh-v1.0, is a burn. Sinks are credit-only: they receive records but are never debited and never consolidated. The FirstGM burn transaction is not credited to the zero address. Burns do not reduce edition sizes.
network.tdh.spec.s4.title: 4. Day, snapshot and whole days
network.tdh.spec.s4.body: Day N is the number of days since January 1, 1970; it closes at N × 86,400 seconds, 00:00 UTC. A date names a day only when it is exactly eight digits of a real calendar date. The snapshot block is the last block before that moment on the finalized chain, and the day has no result until the next block is finalized too. Ages are whole days of the registry’s day_s, 86,400 seconds, measured to the snapshot block’s time. Example: the upload dated 2026-10-11 is day 20,737, boundary 1,791,676,800.
network.tdh.spec.s4.binds: The result binds (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash).
network.tdh.spec.s5.title: 5. Eligibility, editions, rates and seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.title: 5.1 Eligibility
network.tdh.spec.s5-1.body: Memes and Gradients count when their first mint, of any amount, is at least eligibility_min_age_s (86,400 s) before T; a transfer from the zero address to itself is not a mint. NextGen tokens count when minted at or before B. n_memes is the number of eligible Memes, a count.
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.title: 5.2 Editions and floors
network.tdh.spec.s5-2.body: Burns do not reduce an edition. FirstGM’s edition is adjusted by −2,588. A Meme with fewer than 300 copies gets a floor, its claim’s totalMax capped at 310, and its edition is the larger of the floor and the minted count, because the final top-up airdrop takes it to 310, above The Memes’ 300-copy minimum (the Nakamoto Threshold). From 300 copies on there is no floor. A Meme with no claim has no floor. totalMax is a 32-bit number, read at the snapshot block through an adapter that P53 §11.3 pins. A Meme with an effective edition of 0 is eligible but has no rate, and holding a copy of it makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.title: 5.3 Rates
network.tdh.spec.s5-3.body: Meme i: RATE(H, E[i]). Gradient: RATE(H, G), at least the registry’s gradient_rate_minimum (1.00), G = Gradients minted at or before B. NextGen token t: RATE(H, N_c), c = t div 10^10, N_c = tokens of collection c minted at or before B. With no eligible Meme, H = 0: Gradients get the 1.00 minimum and NextGen 0.
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.title: 5.4 Seasons
network.tdh.spec.s5-4.body: Seasons come from the registry’s season_starts, the first Meme id of each season: 1, 48, 87, 119, 152, 181, 213, 246, 279, 311, 343, 375, 407, 439, 477, 516, 556. The list must start at 1 and strictly increase, or the registry is invalid. A season is listed for a day when its first id is at most n_memes; the highest listed is current. Seasons 1 to 20 carry a 0.05 bonus; a season pays when it is not current and its bonus is positive. A new season must be added, as a new rule version, before its first card becomes eligible.
network.tdh.spec.s6.title: 6. Consolidation
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.title: 6.1 Events
network.tdh.spec.s6-1.body: Only delegation events with use case 999, for The Memes or the all-collections address 0x8888…8888, between two different wallets neither of which is a sink, count: a sink is never consolidated. Every event’s position is checked, kept or not; two events at one position make the input invalid. Expiry, allTokens, token id and update events are ignored.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.title: 6.2 Pair state
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.body: Each unordered pair of wallets has at most one row. A registration in one direction is pending; the other direction confirms it. The collection does not partition the state.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.machineDesc: Three states: no row, pending from a to b, and confirmed. REGISTER(a, b) creates a pending row; REGISTER(b, a) on a pending row confirms it. REVOKE on a confirmed row returns it to pending in the other direction; REVOKE by the registering side of a pending row deletes it.
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.title: 6.3 Identities
network.tdh.spec.s6-3.body: Confirmed pairs, newest first, grow cliques of at most 3 wallets in which every pair is confirmed; a wallet joins at most one.
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.title: 6.4 and 6.5 Effective state and identity key
network.tdh.spec.s6-4.body: The grouping after all events up to B applies to the whole history of the day’s calculation. An identity’s key is its sorted lowercase addresses joined by “-”.
network.tdh.spec.s7.title: 7. Holdings
network.tdh.spec.s7.body: First an underflow test counts each wallet’s copies over the transfers before netting: a send of more than the wallet holds makes the input invalid. Then each transaction’s movements of each token are netted: every address’s net change, a sink’s included, with senders and receivers paired in ascending address order. The netted transfers are replayed in canonical order into a list of acquisition times per wallet and token; sends take from the end, and age carries only between wallets of one identity.
network.tdh.spec.s8.title: 8. Arithmetic and scores
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.title: 8.1 Rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-1.body: RATE equals half-up of 100n/d except at an exact half cent; with H = 3,941 that happens only for editions 8, 40, 56, 200, 280 and 1,400. The Gradient minimum comes from the registry.
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.title: 8.2 Base
network.tdh.spec.s8-2.body: Multiply the rate in cents by the whole days and round half up to a whole TDH. This equals the old backend’s two-step rounding.
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.title: 8.3 Boost
network.tdh.spec.s8-3.body: A record holds a token when the token is eligible and the balance is positive, whatever the copies’ ages. ADD’s first term and ratio come from the registry, and ADD stops growing once it reaches the limit of its rounded values; a program derives that point from the registry and must not hard-code it. For tdh-v1.0: ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 for n ≥ 33. The cent rounding never meets a tie.
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.title: 8.4 Final
network.tdh.spec.s8-4.body: FINAL is computed per token; a record’s final is the sum. Ties round down only for some boosts and some bases, the smallest being base 25 at 1.14.
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.title: 8.5 Totals
network.tdh.spec.s8-5.body: The total is the sum of identity finals, never of wallet finals. A second total leaves out the sink identities, one per registry sink, since a sink is never consolidated; sinks never enter any consensus weight.
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.title: 8.6 Daily rate
network.tdh.spec.s8-6.body: rate_e4 = beta × the sum of the rates of each copy with at least one whole day, in 10^-4 TDH a day; derived data.
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.title: 8.7 Range
network.tdh.spec.s8-7.body: A day is inside the tdh-v1.0 range when H, G, every N_c, every base × beta and the total are below 2^53, every net movement of section 7.1’s netting is below 2^64 (vector 50), and every balance and raw of a wallet or identity record, per token and in total, is below 2^64 (vector 58). Outside it there is no result. Inside it, hardware binary64 and exact emulation agree, and every output value fits 64 bits.
network.tdh.spec.s9.title: 9. The day’s output
network.tdh.spec.s9.body: The header (N, B, hash(B), T, rule version, registry hash), and per identity its key, wallets, boost and final, with per-token balance, raw, base and final. The per-token final is what card-set credit uses. Wallet records, daily rates and totals are derived. How the result is encoded, and the roots validators sign, are defined in the canonical-encodings and validator documents (P28, P53), to be published.
network.tdh.spec.s10.title: 10. Parameters
network.tdh.spec.s10.body: Every number the rule uses is a parameter of the rule version. tdh-v1.0 is not frozen until launch: changes made before launch, such as D131’s transaction netting and the clarifications of October 15, stay tdh-v1.0. From launch on, a change to a rule or to a parameter is a new rule version with its own first cycle.
network.tdh.spec.s10.name: Name
network.tdh.spec.s10.hashNote: Recomputed with the Python reference; conformance vector 28 checks it. H here is the hash function of the canonical encodings (P28, a validator design document to be published), not the largest edition.

network.tdh.spec.s11.title: 11. Where TDH-v1 differs from the old backend
network.tdh.spec.s11.body: Nineteen differences, each with what the old backend did, what TDH-v1 does, the measured effect and the decision. On the replayed cycle none changes a value: the only one that did, DEV-2, came from tokens sent out and back within one transaction, which D131’s netting removes.

network.tdh.spec.s13.title: 13. Conformance
network.tdh.spec.s13.body: A program conforms when it reproduces every one of the 89 conformance vectors (01 to 88, and 12b, as of f840096) and, for a real day, the reference implementation’s output from the same inputs. When several rules make an input invalid, any of them may reject it: a vector of an input with no result asserts only that there is none. The Python reference and the Rust reference pass all 89. The Rust core and program B pass the 75 of P26’s fourth round in the validator’s current code, merged on October 15, and have yet to follow the fifth; the version of the Rust core the daily job runs passes the 51 it was ported with. The vectors added since change no value of the October 11 cycle.
network.tdh.spec.decisions.title: Decisions referenced
network.tdh.spec.decisions.intro: The owner’s decisions these pages cite, in brief. The decision record itself is not yet published.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D112: Validator v1 agrees on TDH once a day, peer to peer: each validator computes TDH-v1 with the Rust core, signs the result and compares it with 6529.io.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D116: The validator code is licensed under Apache 2.0 and is published, with the ported TDH-v1 core and its conformance vectors, before the first outside operator runs it.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D118: Every validator checks each block’s events against Ethereum’s block headers, and the headers against a finalized block its own light client follows; a node that cannot complete the checks does not sign.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D119: Two separately written programs, A and B, are to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s own history in two different zero-knowledge virtual machines; both are being built.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D121: One TDH formula everywhere: 6529.io, its backend and the validators compute identical TDH with the validators’ Rust core; the open deviations are settled as listed in section 11.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D125: Every validator computes TDH with two separately written implementations before it signs, and does not sign if they disagree; anyone can add the Python reference as a third.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D128: A minimal Ethereum contract records a day’s result once both programs’ proofs verify; built and tested, deployed only when the owner approves.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D130: A new validator may take the TDH history from the network’s agreement, or check all of it itself.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D131: Ownership is read at transaction boundaries: within one transaction, each wallet’s movements of each token are netted. P26 §7.1 carries the exact rule.
network.tdh.spec.decision.D132: From October 16, 2026 the Rust core and the Python reference run daily beside 6529.io’s backend and are shown side by side; 6529.io switches to the Rust result about one week later, around October 23, 2026.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.title: Evidence
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.title: Replay of 2026-10-11
network.tdh.spec.evidence.replay.body: From the live per-token inputs, TDH-v1 reproduces all 132,481 wallet-token bases and every wallet and identity value. From the 388,335 indexed transfers it reproduced 10,278 of 10,280 identities and 11,128 of 11,130 wallets before D131; the two others were tokens sent out and back in one transaction (DEV-2). With D131’s netting it reproduces all 10,280 identities and 11,130 wallets. The validator’s own Ethereum ingestion later read the raw logs from each contract’s deployment, with the history not yet fully checked: on them the Python reference with netting gives 2,061,888,816, the live total, and equals every live identity and wallet, and the second implementation agrees on every record. The input rules written out later, on October 15 and 16, change nothing on that input: its 414,007 logs pass every position and header-order check, every value is in its type, and the transfers of each log share their contract, sender and recipient.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.cleanRoom.body: The Rust reference, written from the specification and the documents it cites without opening the Python reference or the backend’s code, recorded 23 places where it had to choose (2 high, 11 medium, 10 low). P26 now states a rule for every one; only the state-read adapter for edition floors (F-10) stays open.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.comparison.bod: From independent inputs (Ethereum logs, history not yet fully checked), the Rust core was compared with 6529.io’s published files in every compared field. Before D131: 10,280 of 10,282 identities and 11,131 of 11,133 wallets equal each day; the two others were tokens sent out and back within one transaction (DEV-2). With D131’s netting: all 10,282 identities and 11,133 wallets, with totals equal to the uploads’ (2,070,436,337 and 2,073,214,934). Ranks, the balance and set-count columns (BUG-15) and display fields are not compared.
network.tdh.spec.amended: Changed six times on October 15, 2026, and once on October 16. Edition floors were limited to Memes below 300 copies; transaction netting (D131) entered section 7.1 and was then made uniform; and four rounds wrote out the input rules that the Lean model, the four-way differential tests and their reviews asked about: log positions, logs given raw or decoded, and transfers at one log position sharing contract, sender and recipient (3.1), value types and how values are written in JSON (3.2, 10), cycle dates and the cutoff block in the header set (4.1, 4.2), ZERO to ZERO is not a mint (3.4), the claim limit’s type (5.2), a sink is never consolidated (6.1), the bound on balances (8.7), and a registry that programs read in full, with its constraints (10). The conformance vectors grew from 36 to 89.

network.tdh.spec.symbols.intro: The letters the rule uses, and where each is defined.
network.tdh.spec.symbol.M: The cycle’s boundary, N × 86,400 seconds: 00:00 UTC
network.tdh.spec.symbol.B: The snapshot block: the last finalized block before M
network.tdh.spec.symbol.T: The snapshot block’s timestamp; ages are measured to it
network.tdh.spec.symbol.days: Whole days, of the registry’s day_s, from an acquisition time a to T
network.tdh.spec.symbol.H: The largest effective edition among eligible Memes
network.tdh.spec.symbol.G: Gradients minted at or before B
network.tdh.spec.symbol.Nc: NextGen collection c’s tokens minted at or before B
network.tdh.spec.symbol.net: Address w’s net movement of one token in one transaction
network.tdh.spec.symbol.raw: A token’s whole days, summed over its copies
network.tdh.spec.symbol.base: Rate × raw, rounded: a token’s TDH before the boost
network.tdh.spec.symbol.sets: Full sets: the smallest balance of any eligible Meme, when every one is held
network.tdh.spec.symbol.B64: The nearest binary64 number; it decides ties
network.tdh.spec.symbol.SINKS: The registry’s sinks: the zero address and 0x…dead in tdh-v1.0
network.tdh.spec.s3.decoding: The event signatures and their topic hashes are in section 2.
network.tdh.spec.s7.property: The rule’s property: the acquisition stacks depend only on each transaction’s net movement of each token per address. Inserting, removing or reordering steps inside a transaction that leave every net movement unchanged changes no stack (vectors 45 to 47). The Lean model proves this for the stacks, for two inputs whose transactions correspond one to one and in order. A token’s balance and raw days are read from its stacks, so they stay the same for every token whose eligibility the change leaves as it was; that follows from section 7.2’s definitions, and the Lean model does not prove it separately.
network.tdh.spec.decision.legend: All settled by D121; DEV-2 amended by D131. Adopted: TDH-v1’s rule, which changed no value on the replayed cycle. Spec wins: on-chain order across transactions, netting within one. Old behavior kept: TDH-v1 keeps the backend’s behavior. Kept, not in consensus: sink records stay, and never count toward consensus weight.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t1: No row, then REGISTER(a, b): pending, registered by a.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t2: Pending, then the other wallet registers back: confirmed.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t3: Confirmed, then either wallet revokes: pending again, as the other wallet’s registration.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t4: Pending, then the registering wallet revokes: no row.
network.tdh.spec.s6-2.t5: Confirmed, then the confirming direction registers again: still confirmed, with a newer position.
network.tdh.spec.s3-1.title: 3.1 Log selection and positions
network.tdh.spec.s3-1.body: The inputs are every log of the four event contracts up to the snapshot block, ignored logs included, each exactly once. A log that a reorganisation marked removed is not an input. A log’s place on chain is its block and its index in that block; one log given twice, two logs claiming one place, or a transaction index that falls as the log index rises makes the input invalid. A log is given raw or decoded, never both, and the transfers at one place come from one log, so they share its contract, sender and recipient. These checks run on the inputs, before delegation events are filtered and before transfers are netted.
network.tdh.spec.s3-2.title: 3.2 Decoding
network.tdh.spec.s3-2.body: Three transfer events yield transfers: The Memes’ TransferSingle and TransferBatch, and the ERC-721 Transfer of Gradients and NextGen. Each must be the canonical Solidity encoding, byte for byte; anything else is malformed and the input has no result. Events with other signatures are ignored but still count as inputs. All transfers of one transaction carry one timestamp and one transaction hash. Every value has a type, block numbers and timestamps 64-bit and token ids and amounts 256-bit, and a value outside its type is malformed wherever it is. An amount of 2^64 or more makes the input invalid up to the snapshot block; after it, a transfer is not an input. Values written in JSON are written one way: canonical integers with no −0, never a number as a string, and map keys in canonical decimal; any other form has no result.
network.tdh.spec.s3-3.title: 3.3 Order
network.tdh.spec.s3-3.body: Zero-amount and self transfers move nothing but are kept, because a zero-amount mint is how a card is created. Transfers in different transactions keep on-chain order, even within one block. Within one transaction, each token’s movements are first netted (section 7.1); the edition counts, the underflow test and the position checks read the transfers before netting.
network.tdh.spec.s3-4.title: 3.4 Mints, burns and sinks
network.tdh.spec.s4.order: Header timestamps strictly increase along a valid chain, and every implementation checks it the same way: over every header it reads for the day, adjacent or not. A set that breaks the order anywhere gives no result. The set always holds the snapshot block at its own time, so a log below it stamped at that time or later, or the snapshot block stamped otherwise, makes the input invalid. A decoded transfer at or before the snapshot block stamped after its time contradicts the same order, so it also makes the input invalid.
network.tdh.spec.s7-1.title: 7.1 Acquisition stacks
network.tdh.spec.s7-2.title: 7.2 Per-token values
network.tdh.spec.s7-2.body: For each eligible token a wallet holds: its balance is the number of copies, its raw days the sum of each copy’s whole days, and its base the rate times the raw days, rounded. Tokens that are not eligible contribute nothing, not even balance.
network.tdh.spec.s7-3.title: 7.3 Records
network.tdh.spec.s7-3.body: A wallet has a record when it holds an eligible token or belongs to a group; an identity has a record when one of its wallets does. An identity’s balance, raw days and base are the sums of its wallets’, and its base is never recomputed from merged days. Boost and final are computed per record, so an identity’s final is not the sum of its wallets’ finals: two wallets with one Gradient each have finals 102 and 102, and their identity, holding two Gradients, 208.
network.tdh.spec.s7.limit: The property stops there. The edition counts read every mint as logged, so a mint and its burn inside one transaction change no stack but can make a token eligible and change editions, rates and seasons. Eligibility decides which tokens a record holds at all, so balances and raw days can change too: in the Lean model’s counterexample I, a wallet with no record gets a balance of 5 and another holder’s final goes from 32 to 60; in counterexample H, another holder’s final doubles, from 800 to 1,600. The underflow test also reads the steps, to decide whether the input is valid (vector 44).
network.tdh.spec.s10.read: Programs read every field of the registry at its type and hard-code none, including the sinks, the day length, the Gradient minimum, ADD’s terms and the point where ADD stops growing, the largest group size, the season starts, the Genesis and Nakamoto ids and the consolidation collections; vectors 59 and 65 run whole days under other values. A registry with a value outside its type is no registry, and one that breaks a constraint below gives no result.
network.tdh.spec.evidence.difftest.title: Four-way differential tests, October 15, 2026
network.tdh.spec.evidence.difftest.body: Generated cycles ran through the Lean model, the Python reference, the Rust core and program B in four rounds: 40,000 cycles, then three rounds of 35,000 cases. The first three rounds’ disagreements became rules in P26 the same day: which inputs are valid (F1 to F3), registry lists that a program could not read or ignored (F4, F5), registry numbers above 2^128 and a cutoff search at the last possible block, both in the Rust core (F6, F7), an event’s default use case, logs marked removed, values outside their type and dates that name no day (E8 to E11). Vectors 51 to 74 pin them. In the third and the fourth round the model and program B agreed on all 30,000 main cases. The fourth, on P26’s fourth round, found two defects in how programs read the vector files, in the Rust core (F8) and the Python reference (F9), and one question for the vector format (E12); P26’s fifth round settled all three on October 16 (vectors 76 to 79).
